objective: Remove the pull_request path filter from the workflow that emits the declared required check static-and-cpu-image, replace it with an always-running applicability job plus an always-running verdict job that owns the required check name and reports success, not-applicable or failure, and pin the result with tests that fail on the path-filtered workflow.
decision_supported: Does every pull request targeting main emit a terminal result for the declared required check static-and-cpu-image, and is 'no workflow run was created' distinguishable from 'the job ran and skipped' and from 'the image was actually tested'?
acceptance: The container-full-stack workflow declares no paths or paths-ignore filter on pull_request, so GitHub creates the workflow for every pull request that targets main and the declared required check always emits a result.
The fifteen former trigger patterns survive as data in the always-running static-image-applicability job, which records an applicable output and a human-readable reason on every run.

The expensive build, CPU smoke, dashboard health, SBOM and Grype scan steps move unchanged into static-image-build, which runs only when the decision reports applicable=true, so an image-relevant change is still fully tested.

The required check name static-and-cpu-image is owned by an always-running verdict job with if: always() that reports success for a passing build, not-applicable only when the decision job succeeded and the build was skipped, and failure for a failed build, a cancelled build, or a skipped build whose decision did not run.
A skipped or absent run is never treated as a passing image check: check_release_commit.py still accepts only the success conclusion on a tagged commit.

Tests execute the committed decision and verdict scripts against documentation-only, tools-only, dashboard-only, ruleset-only and image-relevant changes, refuse an empty path policy, and refuse a decision that cannot record its result, so the suite fails on the previous path-filtered workflow.
The branch-protection page documents the trigger policy and the required matrix together and states that adding or removing a path filter or a required check requires owner review.
The workflow YAML parses, every action reference remains pinned to a 40-character commit SHA with a version comment, and the supply-chain scan contract is unchanged.
evidence: Focused pytest output for the trigger-policy, applicability-decision, verdict-job and workflow-pin tests, including the same suite run against the pre-change workflow to show it fails there.
Parsed YAML output showing pull_request carries no paths filter and that static-image-applicability, static-image-build and static-and-cpu-image exist with the recorded needs and if conditions.
Decision-script output for documentation-only, tools-only, dashboard-only and ruleset-only changes reporting applicable=false with a reason, and for a libs change reporting applicable=true.
Verdict-script output for success, failure, skipped-with-successful-decision, skipped-without-decision and cancelled build results, showing which exit code each produces.
check_release_commit.py still refusing a skipped conclusion and reporting a never-created run as missing.
check_task_packet.py --all --base output proving every Git-visible changed path is inside this packet's allowed_paths.
build/verify.sh output comparing the full test suite against build/baseline.txt, run with no other pytest process active.
A strict mkdocs build and a clean whitespace check.
stop_conditions: The change would have to delete static-and-cpu-image from the declaration or treat an absent run as success; that is explicitly forbidden by the issue.

A live GitHub check run would have to be observed to claim the required context now reports; this change establishes the trigger defect and its fix from the workflow and its tests only, so a live run stays unclaimed.
The static-and-cpu-image job fails on main because the base image carries high-severity CVEs; that is a separate defect and is not fixed here.
A concurrent issue would need the same workflow or .github/rulesets/main-protection.json regions edited, so this change stays inside the static image path filter and its documentation.
The expensive image build would have to exceed the documented 90-minute budget for an image-relevant change, which would require an owner-approved applicability policy instead.
A write outside allowed_paths is required, especially to another workflow or to the ruleset declaration.
data_classification: Repository-local workflow configuration, public path names and non-secret check names. No credentials are read, written or logged; the workflow runs with contents: read only.
model_policy: Deterministic Python and shell inside the workflow plus local unit tests; no model inference, no training and no external service calls added by this change.
risks_and_fallbacks: Reporting not-applicable as a passing gate result could be mistaken for a tested image. The verdict job prints the decision reason, writes it to the step summary, and the release checker still refuses any conclusion other than success, so a release cannot ride a not-applicable run.

Moving the fifteen patterns out of the trigger and into a script could drift from GitHub's own matcher. The translation is exercised by tests over the representative documentation-only, tools-only, dashboard-only, ruleset-only and image-relevant paths quoted in the issue.

Every pull request now starts a short ubuntu-24.04 job that checks out the repository and lists changed paths. That cost is bounded and deliberate: a required check that is never created is more expensive than one that always reports.

An unknown or zero base revision (manual dispatch, brand-new branch) builds the image rather than reporting not-applicable, so a run without a comparison fails toward doing the work instead of skipping it.
The image build still fails today because the base image carries high-severity CVEs. That defect is unchanged by this work and remains visible as a failure conclusion, not hidden as a skip.
